The video file lives under longform/ relative to the schedule-tweets root (e.g. 'longform/<slug>.mp4'); prefer no-spaces slug filenames so the dashboard video player resolves cleanly. Each long can be queued to the platforms that have a longform uploader script: rumble (upload-longform-rumble.js), bitchute (upload-longform-bitchute.js), facebook (upload-longform-facebook.js). Each platform has its own independent status flow: pending -> posting -> posted -> failed (or 'skip' to never post there). 'description' is the base description used as the post body/caption (Rumble/BitChute use title+description+tags; Facebook builds its caption from title+description with hashtags stripped). NOTE: the upload scripts currently read the single staged video + metadata.json from the longform/ folder, NOT from this JSON yet — this file is the dashboard queue/record; wiring the scripts to consume it is a future step. REQUIRED: "batch" is the batches.json batch id this longform belongs to (the join key used to compute when a batch is fully posted so its registry status can flip to completed); set null only for pre-registry entries with no registered batch.

longs.title: The Clarity Act Has Three Weeks to Live, and the Robinhood Chain Has No New Retail
longs.description:
The Clarity Act has about three weeks to live, and almost nobody is watching the clock on it.

It cleared Senate Banking 15 to 9 back on May 14th and has been sitting on the calendar ever since with no floor vote scheduled. August 7th is the last day before the Senate leaves for recess. Miss that window and you are looking at recess, then September, then campaign season, and the realistic next shot is 2027.

That matters because Clarity is exactly what the name says. The institutions on the sidelines are not there because they hate crypto. They are there because nobody can tell them what they are allowed to do. Clear legislation gives that money permission to move, and that is the bullish catalyst this bear market has been starving for.

What is blocking it is not crypto policy at all. Democrats want an ethics provision stopping public officials from profiting off crypto they sponsor or endorse, because Trump's annual disclosure showed more than 1.4 billion dollars in crypto income last year. Neither side is dropping it, the bill needs 60 votes, and in mid July those talks collapsed.

In the second half I go through the Robinhood chain memes and say the unpopular thing: there is nobody left to sell to. More than half of everybody in crypto is checked out until October, so every pump on that chain is us trading against ourselves. Cash Cat already ran from around 10 million to a peak north of 150 million and came back to around 80, and the people who bought that top are done with the meta. longs.title: The Bottom Is Being Front-Run, and TAO Under $200 Is the Last Cheap Window
longs.description:
Everyone knows September is red in a post-halving year. So last year everyone sold in August instead, and look what that did: August 2025 closed down 6.5%, then September closed UP 5.16%, the third best September on record.

That is what front-running looks like. Once a pattern becomes common knowledge, the crowd steps in front of it and the crowd's own footsteps move the thing it was trying to predict.

Now the entire four-year cycle crowd has circled October. And that is exactly why October is the one month that almost certainly is NOT the low. If millions of people have all agreed to buy in October, their own buying is what turns those candles green. A bottom is the reddest month on the chart; it cannot also be the month everybody shows up with cash.

longs.title: Kaspa Is Going To 40 Blocks Per Second With DAGKnight
longs.description:
Kaspa already runs at 10 blocks a second, live on mainnet today. The next hard fork, DAGKnight, targets up to 40. This is the real upgrade story: Crescendo took Kaspa from 1 block a second to 10, Toccata shipped programmability this summer, and DAGKnight is the consensus fork that makes everything above 10 blocks per second possible.

DAGKnight is parameterless consensus. GHOSTDAG runs at the speed of a hardcoded worst case latency assumption, so the whole network moves as slowly as that guess. DAGKnight deletes the guess. It measures the real network in real time and runs as fast as the actual internet allows, while staying secure with up to half the network acting malicious, and it opens the door to sub second finality on proof of work.

To be clear, up to 40 blocks per second is a target for the end of this year, not a locked schedule, and the prototype has not hit testnet yet.
